 India look to avoid another batting collapse in series decider
 By: Agencies 
 Date:
 November 15, 2026 
 Share post:
 WhatsApp Facebook X ReddIt Telegram Linkedin 
 Can VISITORS Bounce Back or Will NZ Level the Series?
Today at 7:30 Am 
 India vs new zealand 
 odi 5 of 5 | india lead 2-1 
 Mount Maunganui, Nov 14: Indian batters would be determined to put up a much improved performance against the seaming ball with the series at stake in the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand here on Sunday.
India lead the series 2-1 despite their second heaviest loss in ODIs here on Friday.
The Indian batters came a cropper in seaming conditions with Matt Henry effectively sealing the game for his team in his opening over by striking thrice.
India need to get better on pace friendly surfaces as they could get similar conditions in the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.
Considering the collective failure of the batting line-up, it would not be fair to single out an individual.
Having said that, Rohit Sharma and Shreyas Iyer, who had a forgettable captaincy debut, are yet to make an impact in the five-match series. While Henry squared Rohit up with a beauty, Iyer was caught in the crease against a sharp incoming delivery.
For one format players Rohit and Virat Kohli, the game presents a final opportunity to enthral the crowd on probably their last tour of New Zealand.
Kohli too had no response to Henry’s magic on Friday night. The team collapsing to 89 all out in 26.4 overs while chasing 334 did not go down well with head coach Gautam Gambhir.
“These are conditions which are going to be closest to what we might get during the World Cup. The bigger concern is not the runs. It’s how quickly we got bundled out, around 26 or 27 overs. That is something which is always a concern,” said Gambhir. Captain Iyer said conditions changed drastically in favour of the bowlers in the second innings but there was a stark difference in the powerplay performance of pacers on either side.
While New Zealand reduced India to nine for four in the sixth over, the Indian pacers were not able to make inroads in the opening powerplay. Gurnoor Brar went for runs and so did Auqib Nabi, though they did take a couple of wickets each.Playing his first game of the series, Kuldeep Yadav was taken to the cleaners by Will Young. Kuldeep, who has hardly got game time on the tour, would be desperate to make an impact if he gets to play again.
Released from the Test squad, the left-arm wrist spinner would love to leave New Zealand shores with a performance of repute.
New Zealand, on the other hand, find themselves in another must-win situation as they aim to draw the series.Opener Tim Seifert may have resurrected his career with a fifty in the fourth ODI, while Young, who was dropped twice in the slip cordon, went on to make a fine hundred.The Indian pacers will need to stop the openers from taking the game away from them in the first 10 overs.It remains to be seen if uncapped Brett Randell gets a game at the Bay Oval.
New Zealand have not lost a series at home in seven years and therefore will have plenty to play for against a wounded yet formidable opponent. (PTI)
